# Florence 1490 – Metallurgy & materials

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Copper smelting and bronze** [`copper_bronze`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copper_bronze.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Florentine founders cast bells, guns and large statues by lost wax. Copper comes from Tuscan mines and Germany; tin is imported from Cornwall via Flanders. Local: Bertoldo di Giovanni; the late Verrocchio's workshop (Lorenzo di Credi); copper mines of Montecatini Val di Cecina and Massa Marittima.
- **Bloomery iron (wrought iron, forging, carburising)** [`bloomery_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloomery_iron.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Elba ore, owned by the Appiani lords of Piombino, is smelted with charcoal in water-powered ironworks on the Maremma coast and in the Pistoia hills. Local: Elba (Rio mines); ferriere of the Maremma and Pistoia mountains; Arte dei Fabbri.
- **Hardening and tempering steel** [`steel_heat_treatment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steel_heat_treatment.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Armourers and cutlers harden and temper by colour and by secret quenching recipes (urine, radish juice). That carbon makes steel is unknown. Local: Arte dei Corazzai e Spadai (armourers and swordsmiths). Elsewhere: Milan, the leading armourers (Missaglia).
- **Cementation (blister) steel and case hardening** [`cementation_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cementation_steel.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Smiths case-harden files and tools in charcoal, horn and salt. Converting whole bars in sealed chests is not done; good steel is bought from Brescia and Styria. Elsewhere: Brescia and Bergamo valleys, natural steel; Styria.
- **Blast furnace and cast iron** [`blast_furnace_cast_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blast_furnace_cast_iron.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Brescian masters ran a casting furnace at Este-held Fornovolasco by 1480 with mixed results. Waterworks continued in 1490. The rebuilt ducal furnace produced in 1497. Local: Fornovolasco ironworks, Este Garfagnana. Elsewhere: Brescia and Bergamo valleys; Liège and the Rhineland.
- **Smelting iron with coke** [`coke_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coke_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Tuscan ironworks depend on charcoal. A coke furnace would need suitable coking coal, a reliable supply and experience running a blast furnace. Elsewhere: China, coal in iron smelting since the 11th c..
- **Puddling and rolling (wrought iron from pig iron with coal)** [`puddling_wrought_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/puddling_wrought_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Lombard finers already convert pig iron with charcoal. Puddling would require a supply of pig iron and a different furnace and fuel system. Elsewhere: Lombard valleys and Liège, charcoal finery forges.
- **Crucible steel (wootz, Huntsman's cast steel)** [`crucible_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crucible_steel.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept high. Watered 'Damascus' blades reach Italy through Venice and are admired; how they are made is a mystery. Local crucibles and furnaces fail below the heat needed. Elsewhere: India and Persia, crucible steel ingots.
- **Bessemer steel (cheap bulk steel)** [`bessemer_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bessemer_steel.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium

- **Alloy, tool and stainless steels** [`alloy_stainless_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alloy_stainless_steel.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Chromium, nickel, tungsten and manganese are unknown as metals.
- **Refractories (fireclay, crucibles, furnace linings)** [`refractories_fireclay`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refractories_fireclay.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Glassmakers and goldsmiths make their own pots and crucibles from selected clays; these limit furnace heat. Finding a good fireclay is a prospecting job. Local: glass furnaces of the Valdelsa; potters of Montelupo and Impruneta. Elsewhere: Hesse (Großalmerode), the best crucibles in Europe.
- **Brass and metallic zinc** [`zinc_brass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zinc_brass.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Brass is made by heating copper with calamine, and mostly imported as sheet and wire. Nobody knows calamine holds a metal; zinc boils away unless condensed in a closed retort. Elsewhere: Milan and Nuremberg, brass goods; Zawar in India, metallic zinc.
- **Cupellation, parting and assaying of silver and gold** [`cupellation_assaying`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cupellation_assaying.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. The mint guards the florin's fineness by touchstone, cupellation and parting with aqua fortis or salt cementation. The most quantitative craft in the city. Local: Zecca (mint); goldsmiths' section of the Arte di Por Santa Maria; silver-lead mines of the Colline Metallifere.
- **Mercury and amalgamation of gold and silver** [`mercury_amalgam`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mercury_amalgam.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Goldsmiths fire-gild bronze with gold amalgam and breathe the fumes. Mercury is not yet used to win silver from ore. Quicksilver ointments treat skin diseases. Local: goldsmiths and gilders; apothecaries (mercury). Elsewhere: Almadén (Spain); Idrija (found 1490).
- **Lead is a cumulative poison** [`lead_hazard`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lead_hazard.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Vitruvius' warning is in print (c. 1486) and ignored. Lead white is the standard face paint and pigment; lead glazes, pewter and litharge-sweetened wine are everyday. Local: potters; painters' workshops; apothecaries (biacca).
- **Soldering, brazing and tinning** [`soldering_tinning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soldering_tinning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Goldsmiths, plumbers and coppersmiths solder, braze with borax and tin copper pots. Tinplate is imported from Germany.
- **Pottery, kilns and fired brick** [`fired_brick_ceramics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fired_brick_ceramics.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Brick, tile and terracotta are a major local industry; tin-glazed maiolica and the Della Robbia glazed sculpture are at their height. Local: Impruneta (brick, terracotta); Montelupo (maiolica); Andrea della Robbia's workshop.
- **Porcelain** [`porcelain`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/porcelain.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept high. Chinese porcelain can be examined in the Medici collection. Sultan Qaitbay of Egypt sent Lorenzo porcelain vases in 1487. Local potters lack the manufacturing recipe. Local: Medici collection in the Palazzo Medici. Elsewhere: Jingdezhen (China).
- **Glassmaking and glassblowing** [`glassmaking`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glassmaking.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tuscan glassmakers come from the Valdelsa and make drinking glasses, flasks and apothecary ware. Fine work is bought from Murano. Local: glassmakers (bicchierai) of Gambassi and Montaione; Florentine glass shops. Elsewhere: Murano.
- **Colourless and optical glass (cristallo, lead crystal, plate)** [`clear_glass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clear_glass.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Cristallo is Murano's secret (purified soda ash, quartz pebbles, manganese); Venice forbids its masters to leave. Even cristallo has bubbles and streaks that limit lenses. Local: Florentine spectacle makers. Elsewhere: Murano, Barovier workshop.
- **Glass mirrors (tin amalgam and silvering)** [`glass_mirrors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glass_mirrors.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Polished metal and small backed glass mirrors are available. Producing a large, flat, evenly backed glass plate would challenge local makers. Elsewhere: Nuremberg, convex glass mirrors.
- **Hydraulic lime, Roman concrete and Portland cement** [`hydraulic_cement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_cement.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Masons line cisterns with lime and crushed brick; Vitruvius and Alberti (printed Florence 1485) describe pozzolana from Naples and Lazio. Burning true cement clinker is hard. Local: architects (Giuliano da Sangallo); Vitruvius and Alberti in print.
- **Reinforced concrete** [`reinforced_concrete`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reinforced_concrete.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Iron tie rods and chains in masonry are familiar (Brunelleschi's dome). Iron is hand-forged and dear; Roman-style concrete without iron is the realistic step.
- **Papermaking** [`paper`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Rag paper from water-powered mills is plentiful and feeds the presses. Rags are the bottleneck. Local: paper mills of Colle di Val d'Elsa; Fabriano; cartolai (stationers) of Florence.
- **Preparing textile fibres (wool, flax, cotton, silk)** [`textile_fibres`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/textile_fibres.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Merchant firms organise wool production across town and countryside. Spinners work by hand, and water-powered fulling mills serve the cloth trade. Local: Arte della Lana; fulling mills on the Arno; wool from Spain and the Abruzzi.
- **Tanning leather** [`leather_tanning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/leather_tanning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tanners work by the Arno with oak bark, myrtle and sumac; alum-tawed white leather too. A stinking, low-status trade. Local: tanners (conciatori) near Santa Croce; Arte dei Cuoiai e Galigai.
- **Aluminium** [`aluminium`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aluminium.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Alum is traded by the shipload, but nobody suspects a metal in it.
- **Wood tar and pitch** [`wood_tar_pitch`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wood_tar_pitch.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Pitch for the galleys comes through Pisa. Local: Casentino and Apennine forests; Maremma woods.
